stage: Observed SDK owned-producer failure diagnostics and actual identity preflight

observedFailure.cause: Not established; available exit code and stack frame cannot distinguish trust, identity selection, ACL or signing-format failure.

realImplementation: Any failed public tool prints bounded stdout/stderr, public argv and real exit status to stdout; existing wrapper already captures that stdout in always-uploaded sdk-producer.log even before stage-sdk-fixture.

Per-stream raw capture publication is capped at 65536 bytes, known owned passwords are replaced before truncation, PEM private-key tails are suppressed; private-input process streams/argv are never directly emitted.
Importer public status accepts only fixed stage and OSStatus schema or exact complete public fingerprint/count/proof fields. Missing, extra, wrongly typed, oversized or private stdout is suppressed.

Actual import item identity and an independent SecItemCopyMatching restricted to the one owned Keychain must each match expected leaf DER; expected root/leaf must actually be present in that Keychain.

Private SecKey handle public representation must match the leaf certificate key; the actual key signs a fresh owned challenge and the certificate public key verifies it. No private SecKey representation is exported.
Only current importer and /usr/bin/codesign are granted trusted-app ACL access; importer runs noninteractive. Its self-test never asserts that another codesign process has exercised its ACL.
The actual security find-identity query is restricted to this owned Keychain and emits bounded public observations without converting it into codesign success.
Cleanup failure has its own public status and does not replace the original generation exception; no success manifest is fabricated after a failed tool.

independentReview.scope: Read-only new two-source public output/Swift public API/CF types/actual identity and key preflight

preservedSemantics: Same certificate construction/owned root/leaf extensions and generic trust scope
No explicit trust-setting or search-list override
Same five-file producer source closure and public output allowlist; diagnostics go only to existing stdout log

primarySources.usedFor: Imported item dictionaries can return identities, certificate chains and trust objects; success alone is not proof of later codesign execution.
Import target Keychain and initial SecAccess ACL are explicit importer inputs.
Owned/self-created CAs can exercise signing machinery; subsystem authorization and trust are separate. No reason to mutate global trust from exit1.
A keychain-file argument limits identity lookup; keep actual owned file scope explicit.
Only actual OSStatus-domain CFError codes become public OSStatus diagnostics; no arbitrary userInfo is printed.

limitations: Original codesign stderr was never uploaded and cannot be reconstructed. This stage fixes observation and preflight gaps, not a proven underlying cause of codesign exit1.

The six portable cases execute real Python child processes to test failure/publication boundaries. They do not run or mock success of Apple codesign, the Swift importer, Security/Keychain or any native App tests.
Swift syntax parsing does not establish standalone swiftc typechecking, macOS Security API acceptance or whether the actual SDK-produced framework signs.
Actual codesign, exact detached-CMS/OpenSSL proof and complete native tests still need a root-controlled related SDK checkpoint; no cloud action was taken here.
No account, real device, real key, pairing record, production IPA or private user data was accessed.
